overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law on four counts: improper executive session subject, failure to follow executive session procedures, a vague notice topic, and an untimely complaint response; it ordered future compliance and release of the executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed a personnel issue (a highway employee's resignation and replacement) in executive session improperly.
allegations.key_passage: The Board's November 25, 2013 executive session discussion of the resignation of Mr. Biagini and the hiring of his replacement did not concern any of the matters enumerated in Purpose 1.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to follow required procedures before entering executive session on November 25, 2013.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Board did convene in open session prior to convening in executive session, it failed to follow the remaining procedural steps.

allegations.summary: The posted executive session topic, 'Executive Meeting (Highway Department personal (sic))', was alleged to be too vague to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: At a minimum, the Board should have stated the executive session purpose on which they relied.

allegations.summary: The Board's response to the Open Meeting Law complaint was late and it did not send the AG a copy of the complaint and remedial action description.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to respond to the complaint in a timely manner.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Release the minutes of the November 25, 2013 executive session within ten (10) days of receipt of the determination, if not already done.
